notes: §1985:XVI.2.3.4 GR3: "When the SEGMENT-LIMIT clause is omitted, all segments having segment-numbers from 0 through 49 are considered as permanent segments of the object program": none is overlaid, so each keeps its last-used state. With no clause every segment is resident at 85 (VisitSectionDefinition admits the number, AlterSwitchEmitter's instance fields hold ALTER state). The witness (no OBJECT-COMPUTER, segment 49 PERFORMed twice) prints FIRST, SECOND. Probes: r4c (no clause; segments 1 and 49 each re-entered after independent segment 99) S1 LATER, S49 LATER; r6c (segments 30, 40, 70, 30 intermixed) SB LATER; class c the segment-number at --std 2002/2023 refused COBOL0902 (r2f); class b r5a SECTION 100 accepted (PB5084, 1985-SR-XVI.3.2.3-1).
